contested_decisions.description: Second-half Palmeiras goal by Alex (after Evair's 54' introduction) disallowed for offside on the assistant's flag. Alex maintains (incl. in his autobiography) TV footage showed him onside; TV Globo commentator and ex-FIFA referee José Roberto Wright first backed the flag, then corrected himself saying Alex was level with the United defence. Jovem Pan calls it 'controversially disallowed'.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: José Roberto Wright (former FIFA referee, TV Globo commentary, per Trivela) - said Alex was level after initially backing flag; Alex (player); Jovem Pan and Trivela journalists
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: A goal denied at 1-0 in a match decided by one goal; if valid it would have equalised.

contested_decisions.description: Three first-half Liverpool appeals for handball in the Sevilla area turned down, most prominently against Daniel Carriço (Sky report: 'Liverpool should have had a penalty ... after Carrico looked to have handled'); another reportedly involved Grzegorz Krychowiak. Klopp listed these among 'four decisive, obvious decisions' against Liverpool.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: no expert assessment found; journalist/manager comments only (Sky Sports match report says penalty should have been given; Klopp)
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: A penalty in the first half at 0-0/1-0 could have given Liverpool a lead/2-0 lead; Sevilla eventually won by two goals.

contested_decisions.description: Dejan Lovren header from a corner ruled out because Daniel Sturridge, in an offside position, was judged to interfere with goalkeeper David Soria. Sports Mole called it correctly ruled offside; Bleacher Report claimed replays showed Sturridge initially onside. Klopp counted it among decisions against Liverpool.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: no expert assessment found; journalists split (Sports Mole: correct; Bleacher Report: questionable); Guardian report (via search summary) said Klopp was wrong about the goals
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: Would have made it 2-0 to Liverpool before half-time; Sevilla won 3-1.

contested_decisions.description: Coke's second goal (Sevilla's third) stood after referee Eriksson overruled his assistant's offside flag, because the last touch came from Liverpool's Philippe Coutinho. Klopp complained; Sky and IBTimes reports describe it as the right call.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: no expert (referee) assessment found; match reporters (Sky Sports, IBTimes, Guardian per search summary) said the decision was correct; Klopp disputed it
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: Made it 3-1 with 20 minutes left; at 2-1 the result was still open.
